implementation: SQLite WAL with synchronous FULL and BEGIN IMMEDIATE; ordinary-user local process controls only

interface.ObserverJournal(path,timeout=0.25,max_re: Open one connection per process. Never inherit an open connection after fork. Errors propagate to the observer adapter.
interface.append(kind,key,payload,source=None): Return sequence, record_sha256, duplicate, durable. Same canonical record/key deduplicates after restart. Different bytes raise ObservationConflict and persist conflict counter. No world action is dispatched.
interface.records(after=0,through=None): Iterator over a fixed committed prefix. Each dict has kind/key/payload/source plus sequence and record/previous/chain hashes. Consume only observation data when rebuilding state.
interface.load_projection(name=\"default\"): Return cursor, state, source_chain_sha256. Missing projection has cursor=0 and state=None.
interface.save_projection(name,through_sequence,st: Atomically commit state+cursor with compare-and-swap. Checkpoint references a committed source prefix.
interface.pending(name=\"default\"): Stream committed observations after the durable projection cursor. No in-memory retry list.
interface.integrity(expected_records=None): Check SQLite structure, record chain, projection checkpoints and conflict counters. Expected count comparison is advisory; complete_capture_proven is always false without external primary manifests.
interface.export(path) / inspect_export(path): Atomic replace publishes complete JSONL export. Interrupted .partial files remain. Inspection distinguishes complete, partial and corrupt without repairing source evidence.

validated_guarantees: One serialized sequence across concurrent producer processes; each producer order is preserved.
Process exit after COMMIT before acknowledgement leaves the observation pending durably and same-key retry is safe.
Process exit during projection transaction leaves old checkpoint and pending records intact.
An export crash before atomic replace preserves the previous complete export; the interrupted prefix is classified partial.
The old ObservedPort wrapper preserved the original response object and one world call while the journal was locked. Observer-only receipt recovery did not repeat that call.
Logical record corruption is reported and rejected on reads/appends; tests do not repair or replace it.
limits: No observer can promise an observation survives process death before durable commit. The world-before-write case performed one independent CPU file effect and recovered zero receipt records.
FULL synchronous SQLite plus process-exit controls is not a tested guarantee against lost disks, faulty fsync implementations, power failure or malicious file rewrites.
The journal has no world action executor. Its integrity output cannot prove all actions/inputs were captured; task-level coverage must compare independent original request/receipt manifests.

A busy/disk/serialization exception can produce an observation gap; fail-open adapters must retain diagnostics and preserve the world result. This module never hides the gap by queuing unlimited records.
Cross-process commit order is observer capture order, not a causal order of concurrent world mutations.
Payload size is bounded and SQLite cache is capped at 2048KiB. tracemalloc excludes SQLite native memory, while lifetime RSS includes imports and earlier cases.
Latency is a single local CPU run with tracemalloc enabled, excludes payload acquisition and projection, and is not a production performance claim.

initial_environment_attempts: System python was absent; system python3 lacked pytest/openpyxl. No test artifacts or dependencies were changed. Existing .venv interpreter was then used successfully.
